what: Brixmor owns about 360 open-air shopping centres across the United States, most anchored by a supermarket or a discount retailer, leased to grocers, restaurants and service businesses.
customers: Supermarkets, off-price retailers, restaurants and service tenants on multi-year leases.
money: tenants' share of taxes and maintenance
moat: Grocery and value anchors that bring weekly foot traffic, in centres bought below replacement cost and steadily redeveloped to raise rents.
risks: A tenant bankruptcy empties space that takes quarters to re-let
22 times earnings for low single digit rent growth
opportunities: A 28.2% net margin and $345M of free cash flow
Rents on expiring leases are being reset well above the old levels
Almost no new open-air retail is being built, and occupancy is near record levels
watch: Leased occupancy and the spread on new and renewed leases.
